paragraphs: Friend, here's the heart of it: Christ set us free, and Paul says STAND FIRM in that freedom. He tells the Galatians not to go back under "a yoke of slavery" (Galatians 5:1). Anyone trying to be justified by the law has been "severed from Christ" (Galatians 5:4). Christ plus a checklist is not a thing. We wait eagerly, through the Spirit, by faith (Galatians 5:5).

So what does matter? "Faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6). The Galatians were running so well, and then somebody got in their way with a persuasion that doesn't come from the One who calls them (Galatians 5:7-8). Paul says it works like leaven: "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9). I know a thing or two about dough, and I'm telling you, you do not want that stuff sneaking into your batch!

Freedom isn't a hall pass to do whatever you feel like. Paul says, "do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh. Rather, serve one another in love" (Galatians 5:13). The entire law is fulfilled in this: "Love your neighbor as yourself" (Galatians 5:14). And if we keep on biting and devouring one another, we'll be consumed by one another (Galatians 5:15). So hold tight to the freedom Christ gave you, friend, and spend it on loving people.
